title: Atomic and prime models: the smallest first-order descriptions

based_on.title: Model Theory Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 84–86 (§7.2, Lemma 7.6, Proposition 7.7, Theorem 7.9 and Corollary 7.11); 89 (Theorem 7.14); notes dated 2018-12-14

summary: Build models whose finite tuples each have one isolating formula, and characterize exactly when a theory has a model that embeds elementarily into every other model.
abstract: Can a theory have a model that must occur inside every other model, with every first-order statement about its elements preserved? Such a model is called prime. For a complete theory in a countable language, its prime models are exactly the countable models in which each finite tuple has its entire description determined by one formula. We show how these isolating formulas let us extend a finite match one element at a time, proving both elementary embeddability and uniqueness. We then construct a prime model whenever every consistent formula can be strengthened to an isolating one. The construction names its eventual elements and explicitly arranges an isolating formula for every finite tuple of names.
